rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance – discrimination ban in rental screening, including source of income
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents may not discriminate in viewing or renting an apartment, or in the terms and conditions of tenancy, based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). Applicants may be selected using any reasonable standard, such as ability to pay rent, only if it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.key_value: Protected categories include source of income (Section 8, public benefits)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing transactions in the City of Cambridge; landlords, sellers and rental agents.
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupied 2-family dwellings exempt; owner occupancy cannot be verified from property data.

rules.penalty: After hearing, the Commission may file a criminal complaint in District Court, levy civil fines of up to $300 per violation, seek injunctive relief in Superior Court, and seek damages, expenses and other relief.
rules.citation: Cambridge Municipal Code ch. 14.04 (Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.conflict_note: Summary page from the Human Rights Commission; protected categories are listed jointly for the Human Rights Ordinance (ch. 2.76) and the Fair Housing Ordinance (ch. 14.04). The page does not give an effective date.
